facts.statement: Sonorasaurus lived during the Early to Late Cretaceous, approximately 112 to 93 million years ago.
facts.quote: Sonorasaurus is a genus of brachiosaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Early to Late Cretaceous (Albian to Cenomanian stages, around 112 to 93 million years ago).

facts.statement: Fossils of Sonorasaurus have been found in southern Arizona, United States.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in southern Arizona, United States.

facts.statement: Fossils were discovered in November 1994 by student Richard Thompson in the Turney Ranch Formation of the Whetstone Mountains in southern Arizona.
facts.quote: Fossilized remains were discovered in November 1994 by geology student Richard Thompson in the Turney Ranch Formation in the Whetstone Mountains, located in the Chihuahua Desert region of the Sonoran Desert in southern Arizona.

facts.statement: The name Sonorasaurus means "Sonora lizard" and refers to the Sonora River in the Sonoran Desert where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: Its name, which means "Sonora lizard", comes from the Sonora River that flows in the Sonoran Desert where its fossils were first found.

facts.statement: Sonorasaurus was declared the official state dinosaur of Arizona on April 10, 2018, following a petition by an 11-year-old student.
facts.quote: On April 10, 2018, Sonorasaurus was declared the state dinosaur of Arizona after 11-year old Jax Weldon sent a letter to Arizona governor Doug Ducey

facts.statement: Adult Sonorasaurus is estimated to have weighed around 16 tons, measured approximately 15 meters in length, and stood 8 meters tall.
facts.quote: it weighed around 16 tons when fully grown, it was estimated to be around 15 metres (49 feet) long and 8 metres (27 feet) tall.

facts.statement: Estimates suggest Sonorasaurus was about 15 meters long, 8 meters tall, and weighed 10 metric tons, roughly one-third the size of Brachiosaurus.
facts.quote: Sonorasaurus is estimated to have been about 15 m long, 8 m tall, and weighed 10 MT, which is about one third of the size of Brachiosaurus.

facts.statement: Ratkevich initially classified Sonorasaurus as a member of the Brachiosauridae family.
facts.quote: Ratkevich initially identified Sonorasaurus as a brachiosaurid.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic studies have failed to reach a consensus on whether Sonorasaurus belongs within the Brachiosauridae or outside of it.
facts.quote: However phylogenetic studies in the following years failed to find a consensus, with some finding it to lie within Brachiosauridae and others outside of it.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Sonorasaurus as Brachiosauridae.
